notebook: PLAN: Build a value-focused sequential train, first splitting light C2-C5 from C6+; then test product/blend branches and refine only high-value bottlenecks. Step 1: establish root split and inspect purity, temperatures and costs.

note: Sharpen the C4/C5 root split and recover the four high-value light and middle blends.
notebook:

Root 60/2.5 was too soft: 1013 mol/s tops vs ideal C2-C4 864, losing C5 overhead. Blends offer most revenue without difficult pure splits. Ideal blend values: C3 ~$63M, C4 ~$176M, C5 ~$611M, C6 paraffin ~$1147M, C6 naphthene ~$397M/yr. Root severity increased; T splits C3/C4, B splits C5/C6+, BB splits C6 paraffins from naphthenes+heavies.

note: Test genuinely sharp C4/C5 and C5/C6 splits while removing the unproductive heavy branch; the three light blends should provide the first revenue baseline.
notebook:

Low-severity columns produced no sales. Root 75/4 gave 1260 mol/s tops and lost most C5 overhead, so R/B must rise substantially. C6-paraffin blend (~$1147M/yr ideal) is largest later target; heavy branch deferred to avoid cost without sales.

note: Simplify to the largest near-term prize: make the root cut C5/C6 and recover the C6-paraffin blend in B, eliminating the unproductive light branch.
notebook:
PLAN: First establish a profitable two-column C6-paraffin plant by cutting C5/C6 at the root and C6 paraffins/naphthenes+heavies below it. Add lighter products only if margins justify them.
Current three-column design has no sales and $958M/yr cost. TB is only 74% C5 and TT is mixed C2-C4, so the light branch is unattractive. The B branch is much closer: BT is 86% C6 paraffin, worth $1021M/yr at spec. Removing the C4/C5 complication should let the same sharp B column exceed 95%, with potential positive net value.

note: Sharpen the C5/C6 cut enough to make the C6-paraffin blend sellable while cutting the very high reflux and boil-up costs.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a profitable two-column C6-paraffin plant by cutting C5/C6 at the root and C6 paraffins/naphthenes+heavies below it. Add lighter products only if margins justify them.
Step 1: obtain the first sellable C6 blend. The previous 100/10 root still leaked enough C5 into BT to hold it at 86%, while costing $560M/yr. Reduce excessive internal traffic and cost but retain a sharp root (90 stages, R6/B5) and an 80-stage R5/B5 product splitter. C6-paraffin tops can be worth roughly $1.0-1.18B/yr at 95%, so this is the fastest route to positive reward. Avoid spending on the heavy and light branches until this works.

PLAN: Build on agent-1's profitable C4/C5 core, then recover the remaining C5 and the high-value C6-paraffin blend with two sequential splits; optimize duties after proving purity.
Agent-1's root sends about 300 mol/s of C5 into B, so directly taking C6 paraffins overhead there cannot reach 95%. Instead B must first split C5/C6, giving a second sellable C5 blend, and BB must split C6 paraffins from naphthenes/heavies. The C6 blend is potentially about $1B/yr, justifying a substantial second splitter. Keep the proven three-column core unchanged and test 70/5/4 followed by 80/5/4.

note: Revert to the profitable blend core and test a 60-stage root at the proven reflux and boil-up, seeking capital savings without the purity collapse seen at 50/3.
notebook:
PLAN: Return to the profitable three-column blend core, reduce root cost without losing either blend, then tune the smaller columns and only add branches with clear positive margin.
The two heavy splitters cost $302M/yr and sold nothing: abandon that branch. R192 earns $104M/yr net. R243 shows that cutting root to 50 stages/reflux 3 saves only $20M but loses C4 revenue and $75M C5 revenue, so the cut is sensitive. Test an intermediate 60-stage root at reflux 4, preserving the proven downstream settings. If purity holds, continue cautious root/duty optimization; otherwise revert and optimize TB.

note: Raise root operating pressure to warm its condenser and reduce refrigeration cost while retaining the proven separation settings.
notebook:
PLAN: Return to the profitable three-column blend core, reduce root cost without losing either blend, then tune the smaller columns and only add branches with clear positive margin. Step: test root operating pressure.
The 60-stage root at reflux/boil 4 is essentially as profitable as R192's 70-stage version, so further stage trimming is unattractive. Its $260.6M/yr cost dominates and may be driven by refrigeration after the 20% pressure drop. Test 10% drop: higher pressure should warm the condenser and may sharply cut utility cost, while preserving the proven downstream splitters. Heavy branch remains abandoned; root reflux below 4 causes C4 loss.

note: Restore the best blend core and trim both downstream columns; their product purities have margin, so lower stages and TB duties may improve profit.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the profitable three-column C4/C5 blend core by trimming downstream capital and duties, then test root/double-effect options only if margin gains remain. Step: reduce T and TB size and boil-up.
Reverting turn 8: root dp 0.1 cost only $14.6M/yr less but lost the C5 blend and $355.6M/yr revenue, so root dp 0.2 and reflux/boil 4 are essential. Best core is root 60/4/4/.2, T 50/2.5/2.5/.1, TB 60/4/4/.1, reward 0.238. Root dominates cost but cannot be cheapened by pressure or modest reflux cuts. Test T 40 stages and TB 50/3/3: both products had comfortable purity, so duty/capital savings may be nearly free. Heavy C6 recovery attempts by others are strongly negative.

note: Restore the proven blend core and cut only the C4/C5 splitter duties modestly, retaining its 60-stage separation margin.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the profitable three-column C4/C5 blend core by trimming downstream capital and duties, then test root/double-effect options only if margin gains remain. Step: restore proven TB staging and make a modest 12.5% duty cut.
Turn 9 showed T40/TB50/3/3 misses both blend specs narrowly (94% C4, 93% C5), so most savings were false economy. Best valid core: root 60/4/4/.2, T50/2.5/2.5/.1, TB60/4/4/.1, reward 0.238; revenue $467M, costs $363M. Root dp0.1 destroys C5 recovery. Try TB60/3.5/3.5: retain original stages/separation margin while cutting reflux and boil-up. If purity remains above 95%, then cautiously optimize T or root double effect. Heavy C6 branches seen from agents 2 and 4 remain strongly negative.

note: Reduce root reflux and boil-up together to lower its dominant energy cost while keeping the same nominal C5/C6 cut and downstream separation settings.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the profitable three-column C4/C5 blend core by trimming duties and capital while protecting both blend specifications. Step: test a balanced 12.5% reduction in root reflux and boil-up, with downstream settings unchanged.
Current best: root 60/4/4/.2, T50/2.5/2.5/.1, TB60/3.5/3.5/.1; reward 0.243, revenue $464.2M, costs $357.8M. TB duty reduction succeeded. T40/TB50/3/3 failed narrowly, so do not combine trims. Root dp0.1 fails, dp changes and double effect have been unhelpful; root energy dominates cost. Test root 3.5/3.5, then either tune T duties or root staging based on purity margin. Heavy C6 branches and higher root boil-up are strongly negative.

note: Copy R529 and move the C3 side draw closer to the condenser, where C4 contamination should be lower, while preserving its C4 bottoms recovery.
notebook: PLAN: Restore R529’s profitable three-blend core, then tune its TT three-product column to make the C3 side draw sellable while retaining the small C4 bottoms product. Step 1: move the liquid side draw upward from stage 20 to stage 10 at the same 55% feed fraction to reject C4 contamination. R529 scores 0.304: C5 $349.4M, two C4 cuts $158.6M, but its C3-rich side is unsold. Feed TT contains about 286 mol/s C3, so a clean side draw could add roughly $600M/yr, dwarfing its column cost. Root at 50/4/4/.2 and downstream T/TB settings are proven; avoid changing them while optimizing TT.

note: Remove the unsellable side draw and operate TT as a straightforward C3/C4 splitter, maximizing saleable C4 recovery while eliminating side-draw complexity.
notebook: PLAN: Keep R577’s profitable three-blend core, but replace its ineffective three-product TT column with a simple C3/C4 splitter. Neither the ethane-rich overhead nor the C4-contaminated side draw sells; removing the side draw should recover essentially all TT C4 in one pure bottoms blend and reduce cost. If successful, tune TT recovery/duty, then consider light-end ethane removal only if its extra product value exceeds cost. Root 50/4/4/.2, T 50/2.5/2.5/.1 and TB 60/3.5/3.5/.1 are proven and expensive to disturb. R577 reward .321; its 45% side draw increased C4 bottoms to $53.6M versus $43.7M at 55%.

notebook: PLAN: Adopt R625’s 25% side-draw plant, then reduce the draw to increase C4 recovery while retaining a sellable C3 side stream. If purity holds, test an intermediate fraction if needed; then trim TT stages/duties only with product margin. Root/T/TB are proven and should remain fixed. R625 earns $566.2M with $381.2M cost (reward .422): TTS is 97% C3 and TTB 95% C4. At 20%, more C4 should reach TTB, but C3 purity and flow may decline.

notebook: PLAN: Adopt R671 (best island, 0.461), then optimize its small ethane/C3 splitter to recover more saleable C3 bottoms. Root/T/TB and TT 25% side draw are proven; retain them. R671 adds $26.7M C3 revenue for $9.5M. Its TTT feed has 182 mol/s but only 104 mol/s reaches TTTB, with 59% C3 still lost in TTTT. Test 50 stages and reflux/boil-up 5: ethane/C3 is an easy split, so higher recovery may repay the modest extra duty. Then consider pressure or smaller-column trims based on margin.

note: Adopt R717's superior low-boil-up C3 recovery, then test a still cheaper asymmetric ethane/C3 splitter while preserving the profitable blend core.
notebook: PLAN: Start from R717 (best island, 0.479) and optimize only the inexpensive ethane/C3 splitter; retain the proven root/T/TB and TT 25% side-draw blend core. R717 showed that low boil-up (1.5) is better than symmetric 3.0 or my 5.0: C3 bottoms rises to 131 mol/s and cost falls. Test 30 stages, reflux 2, boil-up 1 to see whether further duty/capital reduction retains adequate recovery and >95% C3 purity. If it degrades, revert to R717 and tune TT side-draw fraction or root cost.

note: Use the best C3 splitter and raise root boil-up to recover the large, valuable C5 flow currently lost in the unsold heavy bottoms, while watching for C6 leakage.
notebook:

Increase root boil-up from 4 to 5 at fixed reflux/stages to drive more C5 overhead; downstream T/TB should retain the C4/C5 splits. Evaluate revenue versus added duty and C6 leakage. If promising, tune root duty; otherwise restore R765 and make only small proven optimizations.

R765 gives 0.488 with $602.6M revenue. Root costs $260.1M and B has 12% n-pentane plus isopentane. Prior root reductions were disastrous, consistent with C5 recovery being duty-limited. TTT boil-up 1.0 is optimal among tested values.

TTT reflux reduction may save condenser duty while retaining its easy ethane/C3 separation.

Root duty is $260M, so a 5% reflux cut has more upside than further small-column tuning. TTT 0.6 fails C3 purity, 0.7 is optimal known, 0.8 slightly worse. Preserve TB and TT settings.
